newsitem.title: USA: Philosopher attacks Oklahoma jury questionnaire.
newsitem.headline: Philosopher attacks Oklahoma jury questionnaire.

text.p: One prospective juror in the Oklahoma City bombing trial is a philosopher who complained Tuesday that a 40-page questionnaire he was asked to fill out was not intelligently written.
"Some of those questions were badly phrased," the college philosophy teacher who grew up on a farm and listens to conservative talk show host Rush Limbaugh told prosecutor Beth Wilkinson.
Wilkinson had told him that all the prosecutors had wanted to question him. "Every member on our team was fighting to question you and I won," she told him.

Both the trial judge and lawyers for the prosecution and defendant Timothy McVeigh have been questioning potential jurors for two days about their opinions on the death penalty and how much exposure they have had to pre-trial publicity.
Like all other potential jurors, the philosophy teacher was identified only by a number.
The man, who is writing his doctoral dissertation comparing theological research with scientific research, also said he strongly opposes the death penalty.

But after being asked several times if he could consider the death penalty if defendant Timothy McVeigh is found guilty, he said he was willing to consider anything, including "whether or not we may all be dreaming."
The teacher, who chose his words very precisely, said it would take a great deal of persuasion "to get me to that point", refering to imposing the death penalty.
He even wrote a comment in the margin of the questionnaire, saying a question on juror sentiments toward government was not properly explained.
By the end of the questioning, U.S. District Court Judge Richard Matsch said "we're done with this seminar."
McVeigh is charged with bombing the Alfred P. Murrah federal building on April 19, 1995, killing 168 people.
